nodes.title: the Quilumb signature
nodes.statement: The Quilumb system concerns objects called qenjens. There are exactly 5 of them: yuktarn, xilzam, shentu, nyrazt, cloreld. Two operations are written + and |=. One relation is written <~, read as "answers to".

nodes.title: the Quilumb combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x + y for every pair of qenjens is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for |=. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y, x + y is again a qenjen.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x, y, z: (x + y) + z = x + (y + z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y: x + y = y + x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a qenjen xilzam with xilzam + x = x + xilzam = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a qenjen yuktarn with yuktarn + x = x + yuktarn = yuktarn for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y, x |= y is again a qenjen.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x, y, z: (x |= y) |= z = x |= (y |= z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y: x |= y = y |= x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a qenjen cloreld with cloreld |= x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every qenjen x: x |= x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every qenjen x: x <~ x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x and y, at least one of x <~ y and y <~ x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all qenjens x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z |= x) <~ (z |= y) and (x |= z) <~ (y |= z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some qenjen x admits no qenjen y for which x + y and y + x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = yuktarn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every qenjen x: x + x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = shentu, value = cloreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all qenjens x, y, z: if x + y = x + z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = yuktarn, y = yuktarn, z = xilzam, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all qenjens x, y, z: x |= (y + z) = (x |= y) + (x |= z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = shentu, y = shentu, z = shentu, left = shentu, right = cloreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all qenjens x and y: x + (x |= y) = x and x |= (x + y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = xilzam, y = yuktarn, value = yuktarn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all qenjens x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z + x) <~ (z + y) and (x + z) <~ (y + z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = xilzam, y = shentu, z = nyrazt, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: tufal qenjens
nodes.statement: A qenjen x is called tufal when x + x = x.

nodes.title: qenjens that braumb
nodes.statement: Two qenjens x and y are said to braumb when x + y = y + x.

nodes.title: rastdri collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of qenjens is rastdri when x + y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the opalglim of a qenjen
nodes.statement: The opalglim of a qenjen x is the collection of qenjens y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the mithra
nodes.statement: The qenjen xilzam is called the mithra of the system. It is the unique qenjen that leaves every qenjen unchanged under +.

nodes.title: the zammorn
nodes.statement: The zammorn of the system is the collection of qenjens that braumb with every qenjen.

nodes.title: the vexfex
nodes.statement: The vexfex is the collection of all tufal qenjens.

nodes.title: the kaduth of a qenjen
nodes.statement: The kaduth of a qenjen x, written [x], is the smallest rastdri collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a tezwren
nodes.statement: A qenjen f is a tezwren when f <~ y holds for every qenjen y, that is, when the opalglim of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: glimclo qenjens
nodes.statement: A qenjen x is glimclo when x + x equals the mithra.

nodes.title: the korrgel of a qenjen
nodes.statement: The korrgel of a qenjen x is the number of qenjens in its kaduth [x].

nodes.title: the zelopal
nodes.statement: The zelopal of the system is the collection of qenjens whose korrgel is largest.

nodes.title: duthsib pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct qenjens x and y form a duthsib pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the opalglim of the other.

nodes.title: the mithra is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one qenjen e with e + x = x + e = x for every qenjen x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every qenjen unchanged.
Then e + f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e + f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the mithra lies in the zammorn
nodes.statement: The mithra braumbs with every qenjen.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the mithra and x any qenjen.
Then e + x = x and x + e = x.
So e + x = x + e, which is what it means to braumb.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the zammorn.

nodes.title: the zammorn is rastdri
nodes.statement: If x and y both braumb with every qenjen, then so does x + y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the zammorn and let z be any qenjen.
Then (x + y) + z = x + (y + z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each braumbs with everything.
So x + y braumbs with z, and the zammorn is rastdri.

nodes.title: the kaduth of a qenjen is rastdri
nodes.statement: For every qenjen x, the collection [x] is rastdri.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under +.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the kaduth is contained in every rastdri collection
nodes.statement: If S is rastdri and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a qenjen is tufal exactly when its korrgel is one
nodes.statement: x + x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x + x = x then {x} is already closed under +.
So [x] = {x} and the korrgel is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x + x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the korrgel divides the number of qenjens breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every qenjen x, the korrgel of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = shentu, reach = 4, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the kaduth of a zammorn qenjen stays in the zammorn
nodes.statement: If x lies in the zammorn then every qenjen of [x] lies in the zammorn.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zammorn is rastdri.
[x] is the smallest rastdri collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the zammorn is one.

nodes.title: the vexfex is rastdri
nodes.statement: If x and y are both tufal then so is x + y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be tufal.
The claim asks whether (x + y) + (x + y) returns x + y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: opalglims are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the opalglim of x, then the opalglim of y is contained in the opalglim of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the opalglim of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one tezwren
nodes.statement: No two distinct qenjens can both be tezwrens.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <~ h, since h is any object, and h <~ f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a tezwren
nodes.statement: Some qenjen tezwrens the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no duthsib pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct qenjens lie in each other's opalglim.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every qenjen lies in the zammorn
nodes.statement: Every pair of qenjens braumbs.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zammorn is defined by braumbing with everything.
The claim is that x + y = y + x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every qenjen is tufal breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x + x = x for every qenjen x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = shentu, value = cloreld, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some qenjen reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a qenjen whose kaduth is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 4, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x <~ y then y <~ x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = yuktarn, y = xilzam, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the mithra swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e + x equals the mithra for every qenjen x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = xilzam, x = yuktarn, value = yuktarn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the zammorn intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the zammorn then so does x |= y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The zammorn is already rastdri under +.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that |= respects the zammorn as well.
